## **2\) Pick 3 Niches**

Use the Niche Discovery Spreadsheet to define 3 niches for testing.

**Formula:** “I build **\[service\]** for **\[market\]**.”

Examples

* “I build churn-risk detection dashboards for course creators”  
* “I build AI lead-qual agents for staffing agencies”  
* “I build onboarding automations for B2B SaaS companies”

I recommend setting a 20-minute timer for this process. Resist the temptation to overthink this stage. The idea is to have 3 solid niches, test messaging to all 3 and then niche down when you find a winner.

[**Download the Niche Discovery Spreadsheet**](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1zXLFZXqNgil_wQhtlQE2vaC0X7OsHeWcjjU06AyxZmA/edit?gid=0#gid=0)

It’s important to have a strong profile and a system for sending out consistent, quality proposals. ## **4\) Upwork Loom Script**

[**Upwork Loom Script**](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-BLKiN1rimrNeqSINzS8Kx75Xj01TPnbECOwVBnjGBk/edit?tab=t.0)

**Goal:** short, specific, ROI-framed walkthrough that proves you can achieve the desired outcome

**Quick Video Structure**

* Open with a 5-sec intro  
* Name 2–3 specifics you noticed (requirements, edge cases).  
* Show a mini build/diagram and outline exact steps you’d take.  
* Close with next steps and assume the win (propose call, retainer intent).

**Full Script (variables)**

*Intro (0:00–0:05) — open \+ scroll the post*  
“Hey {{client\_name}}, I’m {{your\_name}}. Saw your post for {{job\_title}}—here’s exactly how I’d handle {{job\_description\_excerpt}}.”

*What I noticed (0:05–0:20) — 2–3 specifics*  
“I noted {{specific\_1}} and {{specific\_2}}—plus {{specific\_3\_optional}}. That impacts {{impact\_1}} and {{impact\_2}}.”

*Mini build / plan (0:20–0:45)*  
“Plan is ingest → process → output:  
Ingest: {{source\_or\_platform}} via {{apify\_actor\_or\_uploader}} (triggered by {{http\_request\_tool}}).  
Process: de-dupe in Google Sheets, {{transcribe/parse/generate}} to JSON, write new script/text.  
Output: {{schedule/upload/report}} to {{platforms\_or\_destination}}.”

*Close (0:45–1:00) — next steps*  
“I prefer fixed price so we never go over budget. If you’re open, send two times—I’ll bring scope, milestones, and we’ll ship v1 this week. After that, a light monthly retainer for tweaks \+ monitoring.”

## **6\) Community Lead Gen — One-Page Play (Post \+ DM Templates)**

**Why communities?** You can absolutely land clients hanging out in Slack groups, Skool, Reddit, etc, although it can be a bit of a grind. Our main objective here is building authority and becoming the go-to person in a group for a given subject.

**Rules**

* No direct pitching. Value first; soft, indirect self-promo only.  
* Brand to the room (e.g., “Exploring {{niche}} / learning {{role}}”).  
* Focus: 1 quality community per niche is enough.

**Where to find**

* Skool search by niche/function.  
* Facebook Groups: {{niche}} \+ (community|group|inner circle); target 100–1,000 members.  
* Slack/Discord via Google: best {{niche}} communities \+ (slack|discord).

**Posting cadence**

* Rotate across 3 chosen communities; post 1/day; repeat until 15 posts.  
* Topic \= common pain \+ simple automation (screenshots; Loom in comments).

**Community Value Post — Template (paste-ready)**

*Title (optional): A dead-simple way to fix {{pain}} in {{niche}} (no dev needed)*

I keep seeing {{niche}} teams struggle with {{pain}}. Here’s a tiny automation that fixes it:

**What it does**

* Pulls {{input/source}}  
* De-dupes \+ cleans in {{tool}}  
* {{action/transform}} → drops results to {{destination}}  
* Optional: auto {{schedule/upload/notify}}

**Why it works**

* Cuts {{time/cost}} by {{% or minutes}}  
* Removes {{bottleneck}}  
* Frees {{owner}} from babysitting {{process}}

If helpful, I recorded a 2-min Loom (no pitch, just steps) — I’ll drop it in the comments.

*Soft CTA:* If you try this and get stuck, comment “help” and I’ll share the SOP.

**First Comment (Loom link) — Template**

*Here’s the Loom walkthrough I promised (2 min): {{loom\_link}}. Chapters: 0:00 context • 0:25 flow • 1:15 edge cases • 1:45 next steps. If you want the template/SOP, comment “template” and I’ll post it.*

**DM Templates (copy/paste)**

*For Likes (light touch):*  
Hi {{first\_name}}—appreciate the like on the {{topic}} post. Do you also run {{their\_business\_type}}? Cheers.

*For Comments (warmer):*  
Hey {{first\_name}}, thanks for the comment on the {{topic}} post. Here’s the extra detail you asked for: {{info/link}}. If you want, I can show it live—no pitch. What time works?

*For Inbounds (assume the win):*  
Love it. I’ll map your flow and bring a mini plan. What’s good for a quick call—{{time\_option\_1}} or {{time\_option\_2}}?

[**Community Post Examples**](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1iGJCe-JFJ87v8PhJbz95_KONwQsAwDvR_uynmlPRdTI/edit?tab=t.0)

## **8\) Consultative Sales Call Skeleton**

[**Consultative Sales Call Skeleton**](https://docs.google.com/document/d/18ev7azUnk4vLul8LYPWq08aC3kRZ4auE1D850m8Mf54/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.st6bpmfr8lx2)

# **Consultative Sales Call Skeleton**

### **1\. Build Rapport (2–3 min)**

* Keep it light. The goal is to make them smile once.  
* Example: a quick joke, small talk about their industry, or a compliment on recent work.  
* Transition: *“Alright, you ready to dive in?”*

### **2\. Set the Agenda (1–2 min)**

* Frame the call so they know exactly what’s coming.  
* Script:

  “Here’s how I usually run these calls: first, I want to learn what made you take this call today. Then we’ll dig into your business and the challenges you’re running into. I’ll ask a few questions to get a sense of the size of those challenges — both in time and dollars. If I think I can help, I’ll walk you through what that looks like. At the end, you can decide if it makes sense to move forward. Sound good?”

This creates buy-in and sets up the “pain → investment” flow.

> ### **3\. Discovery (10–15 min)**

* Start broad:

  * *“Why did you decide to book today?”*  
  * *“What’s your main goal for the next 3–6 months?”*

* Dig into pain:

  * *“What’s getting in the way of hitting that goal?”*  
  * *“How have you tried to solve this before? What didn’t work?”*  
  * *“Why now? What’s changed that makes this urgent?”*

* Deep-dive diagnostic:

  * *“Walk me through your customer journey, from first touch to fulfillment. Where are the biggest leaks?”*  
  * *“What’s your current revenue per employee, or ROI per employee? Where do you feel that’s underperforming?”*  
  * *“How much has the company grown over the last year? How far is that from where you want to be?”*

* Quantify the pain in $$$:

  * *“What does that bottleneck cost you right now — in lost revenue, wasted hours, or missed opportunities?”*  
  * *“If this problem was solved, what would it be worth to you in monthly revenue or time saved?”*

### **4\. Transition to Solution (2–3 min)**

* Acknowledge what they shared:

  “Thanks, that gives me a really clear picture. From what you’ve told me, the biggest pain is \[X\], which is costing you roughly \[$\].”

* Check alignment:

  “Is that accurate?”

This ensures you and the prospect agree on the size of the problem before you pitch.

### **5\. Present the Solution (5–7 min)**

* Position your system as the best-fit fix.

* Script:

  “Here’s how I’d solve this. I’ve built similar systems for \[industry/niche\]. The approach is \[describe your templated solution with slight customization\]. This would eliminate \[pain\], save you \[hours/$\], and give you \[desired outcome\].”

* Keep checking in: *“Does this line up with what you were hoping for?”*

### **6\. Frame the Investment (2–3 min)**

* Don’t use “cost” or “price.” Frame it against the pain.

* Script:  
    
  “Based on the scope, this project would be in the neighborhood of \[$X\]. Considering that \[problem\] is costing you \[$Y per month\], this isn’t really a cost — it’s an investment that pays for itself in \[timeframe\].”

* Example: *“You told me missed leads are costing about $15K/month. The system I’m proposing is a one-time $5K investment. That means if it works as designed, it pays for itself in the first couple of weeks.”*

### **7\. Next Steps (1–2 min)**

* Light close, no pressure.  
* Script:

  “Here’s what happens next: I’ll scope this out in more detail and send you a proposal today. You can review it, and if everything looks good, we’ll get started right away. Sound like a plan?”

### **8\. Objections**

* Preempt most objections by qualifying up front.  
* If they hesitate:  
  * *“What’s holding you back?”*  
  * *“Is it the scope, the timeline, or the investment?”*  
* Tie it back to pain:  
  * *“I get it. But if the problem is costing \[$X\] a month, does it make sense to keep waiting?”*

## **10\) Kickoff Call SOP**

[**Kickoff Call SOP**](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wcmcMFucDnv3g3YyY4LBlwe4JDSK0lAOt4_zZ9h6UuE/edit?tab=t.0)

*Hi/introductions/thanks for joining (2 mins)*

*Why we’re here (2 mins)*

* Biggest issue in this space is logistics: 2FA, passwords, permissions.  
* We frontload onboarding live on the call to avoid weeks of back-and-forth. OK?

*Goal for next 30 mins (2 mins)*

* Timelines, communication, expectations.  
* Sign up / grant access to required platforms on-call (handle 2FA live). Questions?

*Timelines*

* Start: {{today}}; Wrap: \~3 weeks. Split into milestones; deliver early if possible.

*Availability (daily updates)*

* One daily Slack update (M–F): status, next steps, blockers. Batch one-off questions. OK?

*Platforms (handle now)*

* Need admin to Asana \+ Slack (example). Share screen if needed; we guide live.

*Wrap-up*

* Questions?

* First update tomorrow.

## **13\) Project Walkthrough — Loom Script (≈10 minutes)**

*0:00–0:20 | Intro & TL;DR*

“Hey {{client\_name}}, it’s {{your\_name}}. Quick walkthrough of {{project\_name}}.  
TL;DR: It {{primary\_outcome}} by doing {{one-sentence\_how}}. No action needed during this video—just watch, then run the two test cases I’ll share at the end.”

*0:20–0:35 | Agenda*  
“Agenda: flow, live run, guardrails, how to edit, next steps.”

*0:35–1:30 | System Overview (plain English)*  
“Think ingest → process → output.

* Ingest: {{source}} (e.g., {{api/drive/form}}).  
* Process: {{steps}} (e.g., de-dupe, transform/transcribe, AI generate, validations).  
* Output: {{destination}} (e.g., {{sheet/db/docs/slides}}, scheduler, Slack/email).  
   Runs on {{orchestrator}}.”

*1:30–3:15 | Live Run (happy path)*  
Trigger: {{manual button/schedule/webhook}}; input: {{sample\_id or file}}. Show outputs:

* {{Artifact 1}} at {{link\_1}} (why it matters)  
* {{Artifact 2}} at {{link\_2}}  
* Notification to {{channel/email}} with summary

*3:15–4:45 | Guardrails & Edge Cases*

* De-dupe by {{key}}  
* Validation for {{bad\_input}} (reject with reason)  
* Retries/backoff for {{rate\_limits/timeouts}}  
* Errors alert to {{channel/email}} (log link)  
* Rollback via {{rollback\_method}}  
* Logging in {{log\_location}}

*4:45–6:15 | What You Can Edit*

* Config: {{config\_link}} ({{thresholds/senders/templates}})  
* Schedule: {{cron/scheduler}} at {{time\_zone}}  
* Templates: {{doc/slide/email\_template\_link}}  
* Destinations via {{setting\_name}}

*6:15–7:00 | Access & Docs*

* Workflow/App: {{primary\_link}}  
* Dashboard: {{dashboard\_link}}  
* Docs: {{one\_pager\_link}} \+ {{sop\_link}}  
* Credentials via {{1Password/LastPass}}

*7:00–7:40 | Performance*  
Run time {{run\_time}} for {{volume}} items; alerts near {{limits}}; tooling {{orchestrator}} \+ {{aux\_tools}}.

*7:40–8:30 | Acceptance Test*

* Test A: {{test\_step\_1}} → expect {{expected\_result\_1}}

* Test B: {{test\_step\_2}} → expect {{expected\_result\_2}}  
   Reply “approved” or list issues by {{acceptance\_date}}.

*8:30–9:10 | Go-Live & Handoff*  
Go-live {{go\_live\_date}} at {{time\_zone}}. I’ll monitor first {{monitor\_window}} runs.

*9:10–9:50 | Support & Care Plan*  
{{warranty\_days}}-day bug-fix; optional care plan ${{price}}/mo.

*9:50–10:00 | Close*  
“That’s it for {{project\_name}}. Reply ‘approved’ or notes; I’ll action today.”
